title: Former top Mountie, guilty of rec centre teen assault, gets conditional discharge
summary: A former high-ranking B.C. RCMP officer has been granted a conditional discharge in an assault case stemming from an incident at the Abbotsford Recreation Centre last summer.

image.caption: Former B.C. RCMP assistant commissioner David Teboul enters the Abbotsford Law Courts on Oct. 28. He has been given a conditional discharge after pleading guilty to one count of assault. (Hunter Soo/CBC News)

blocks.text: A former high-ranking B.C. RCMP officer has been granted a conditional discharge in an assault case stemming from an incident at the Abbotsford Recreation Centre last summer.
David Teboul, 52, must comply with a weapons ban and report to a probation officer
A former high-ranking B.C. RCMP officer has been given a conditional discharge in an assault case stemming from an incident at the Abbotsford Recreation Centre in last summer.

David Teboul, 52, was charged in September with two counts of assault, and another count of assault causing bodily harm by choking, after an off-duty incident at the recreation centre on July 2, 2025.
He pleaded guilty to one count of assault last month, and the remaining charges were stayed.
The court heard that Teboul resigned from his position as the B.C. RCMP's assistant commissioner on July 1.

During a sentencing hearing on Oct. 28, Crown prosecutors played a nearly five-minute-long CCTV video from inside the kids' play area at the recreation centre, showing Teboul pushing, then grabbing, a teenager by the neck.
Teboul previously served as the B.C. RCMP assistant commissioner. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
Reading from an agreed statement of facts, special prosecutor Andy MacKay said Teboul and his wife were attending their son's lacrosse game.

After the game, CCTV video showed their son getting into a verbal altercation with the victim from the other team. Teboul's wife came between them, continuing to confront the victim after her son walked away.
Teboul was beside his wife, watching the interaction happen, before getting involved. He identified himself as a police officer, and told the teen to leave the rec centre or face arrest.

blocks.text: MacKay said Teboul grabbed the victim's neck area for about three seconds, with enough force to lift the youth off the floor.
Another 16-year-old ran to help the victim, but Teboul pushed them away, and grabbed the victim by the neck again for about 15 seconds.
Near the end of the interaction, another unidentified man stepped in. Teboul pushed him away, giving the victim a moment to wrestle Teboul's hands off their neck.

Kier Junos covers B.C.'s Fraser Valley for CBC News in Abbotsford, his hometown. He previously worked as a video journalist for CityNews Vancouver for five years. In 2023, he won the inaugural Emerging Journalist of the Year award from the Radio Television Digital News Association, for his reporting on drug policy and unhoused communities. He has a bachelor of journalism with a minor in economics from Kwantlen Polytechnic University.
